title: Finite-stage Weil representatives and the exact point-heart equivalence
statement:
Fix a prime power $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and let $g_s$ be its geometric Frobenius automorphism. Use the raw rational and common-stage coefficient categories [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], their constructible hearts [def-weil-constructible-heart], Weil pairs [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], and the specified point-fibre functors [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point].
For every finite $E\subset\Omega$ over $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and for $\Lambda=\Omega$, the functor $\omega_\Lambda=H^0\operatorname{Fib}_{s,\Lambda}$ (degree-zero cohomology [def-weil-coefficient-cohomology-modules]) restricts to an exact equivalence from $\Sh_c(s,\Lambda)$ to finite-dimensional $\Lambda$-vector spaces. It preserves and reflects kernels, cokernels, zero objects and short exact sequences. Its identifications with degree-zero fibres are the canonical truncation comparisons; for $E\subset L\subset\Omega$ they commute with the specified scalar/cohomology comparisons, with identity normalization and compatibility under successive extensions.
For every constructible $\Omega$-Weil sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $\operatorname{Spec}k_0$, there exist a finite $E_0\subset\Omega$, an actual object $M\in\Sh_c(s,E_0)$, an isomorphism $\theta:Lg_s^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}M$, and a Weil isomorphism $e:(E_0,(M,\theta))\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal F$. Both inverse identities for $\theta$ and $e$, and the Weil-intertwining identity for $e$, hold at one common finite coefficient stage. The induced fibre identification is $\omega_\Omega(\mathcal F)\cong\omega_{E_0}(M)\otimes_{E_0}\Omega$, with the specified scalar comparison. No continuity condition on the powers of $\theta$ is assumed.

proof.text: Use the rational and common-stage essential-image theorem. Finite dimensionality of each value is the defining property of coefficientFdCohomology and coefficientQbarCohomology. Apply the proved generic exactness-from-essential-image theorem separately to the two functors.

Take the simultaneous rational scalar/truncation squares and common-stage truncation comparisons from the truncation step. Take identity and tower normalization from the scalar step. The remaining change-of-stage equation is exactly coefficientQbarCohomology_changeStage at degree zero.

For the given Weil sheaf obtain simultaneous finite-stage carrier and structure data. Retain each field and arrow. Define fibre as H^0 of the specified common-stage fibre applied to e inverse, followed by zlPointWeilStageOmega at the specified localClosedPoint. The fibre normalization is reflexivity. This supplies every field of the original witness and finishes the conjunction.
